question: Can reviewed multi-file apply, undo, redo and recovery preserve their starting state across host failures, while retaining truthful recovery evidence?
subset: Native Unix journaled UTF-8 regular files and symlinks, including absent and empty files, mode changes, creation and deletion. Cooperative workspace locking.
acceptance: Inject handled failures and process exits before and after staging, publication, synchronization and journal operations.
Read a fresh journal after every failure and resume any pending transaction to its original snapshots.
Refuse changed staged material and unrelated current edits, preserving the pending journal for repair.
Recheck and synchronize restored paths before clearing recovery, including already-restored paths.
Expose transaction, action, failure phase, outcome and observed pending state through CLI JSON.
Check finite publication/recovery decisions against source-anchored executable Lean models.

budgets.fault_scope: Each observed before/after boundary in the deterministic host trace; separate compound-failure and conflict cases.

oracle: Fresh filesystem snapshots of bytes, entry kind, permissions and absence, plus independently specified stack/status expectations; fresh process recovery after injected exit 77.
edit_boundary: fr guide and evidence intent inspect history.rs::install with a one-file scan. Direct edits add host operations, failure contracts, test injection, Lean models and documentation across files; no existing author operation expresses the integrated change.
claims: Finite host-failure corpus, process interruption and tested model agreement. No power-loss simulation, adversarial race elimination, general filesystem proof or live-agent measurement.
